result.summary:
REQ-030 (walk-in registration at the door with in-flow consent and logged capacity override, GitHub issue #33) had RELEASE-VALIDATOR PASS at Step 5 -- the THIRD and FINAL requirement of Phase 6, which RELEASE-VALIDATOR also confirmed makes all three check-in entry points (REQ-028 manual, REQ-029 QR, REQ-030 walk-in) fully coherent: a walk-in-created registration receives a real qr_token on admission (never left absent) and correctly reflects 'already checked in' via either the manual toggle or a later QR scan. Verified the factual claims directly against the real code before writing the status-history note, not from this handoff's summary alone: read apps/bot/src/domain/walkin.ts in full (parseWalkinArgs, validateWalkinFields, normalizePhoneForMatching, decideWalkinOutcome's 7-row first-match-wins table, formatWalkinConfirmMessage/formatWalkinOverrideMessage, parseWalkinMessageFields, commitWalkin's single db.transaction) and apps/bot/src/handlers/walkin.ts in full (makeWalkinCommandHandler + the three callback handlers: makeWalkinConfirmCallbackHandler, makeWalkinOverrideCallbackHandler, makeWalkinCancelCallbackHandler). Confirmed via `git diff master...HEAD --stat -- apps/bot/drizzle apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts` that no schema change exists in this diff. Confirmed via `cat docs/issues/ISS-0026.yaml` that the filed issue (tg_id range collision between checkinQr.forgery.test.ts and walkin.db.test.ts, both starting at 942_000_000, MINOR, non-blocking, currently passing under --no-file-parallelism) is accurately described. Documented precisely, for a future reader, the genuinely novel architectural pattern this requirement introduces: the confirm/override flow carries its collected, not-yet-persisted data (name/company/phone) in the TEXT of the bot's own rendered message (re-parsed via parseWalkinMessageFields(ctx.callbackQuery.message.text) on the confirm/override tap), not callback_data/memory/a DB column -- because S1 forbids writing anything before consent, there is no DB row yet to derive resumable state from at that point (unlike REQ-019's profile form, which already has a row to resume from). This was rigorously security-analyzed and confirmed structurally forgery-proof across the design gate, SECURITY-REVIEWER's Step 2c, and RELEASE-VALIDATOR's own re-derivation: only the bot itself can attach a given callback_data to a message it rendered, so no other party can forge different field values into a confirm/override tap. Also verified: person-matching by phone (normalizePhoneForMatching's digit-strip) reuses an existing profile if getUserIdByPhone finds one, else creates user+profile+registration atomically inside commitWalkin's one transaction, all gated behind consent given in the confirm-tap message itself (formatWalkinConfirmMessage embeds catalog.walkin.consentStatement; the initial /walkin command handler performs zero writes per its own §8.1 step 7 comment). Authorization is requireOrganizerForChapter (REQ-016), never requireEventStaffForEvent (REQ-018/029), re-checked on every tap -- confirmed by reading both callback handlers. Over-capacity requires an explicit organizer confirmation via a second commitWalkin() call with overrideConfirmed=true, audited as registration.walkin_override_admit (vs registration.walkin_admit when seats remain) -- one writeAuditLog call in the same transaction as the write.

Actions taken:
1. Flipped docs/agents/requirements.yaml's REQ-030 entry status: pending -> done. No other field needed correction -- description/acceptance_criteria already matched the shipped mechanism exactly.
2. Appended one 'done' event to docs/status/requirement_status.yaml (append-only; read the file in full across two reads before appending; `git diff --numstat` confirmed 6 insertions / 0 deletions on requirement_status.yaml and 1/1 on requirements.yaml matching only the expected status-field flip, before committing). The note includes a PHASE 6 COMPLETE marker, matching the established convention from REQ-014's Phase 2, REQ-018's Phase 3, REQ-024's Phase 4 and REQ-027's Phase 5 completion notes -- REQ-030 is the third and final requirement of Phase 6 (Check-in at the door: REQ-028 manual, REQ-029 QR, REQ-030 walk-in), all now done.
3. Checked README.md (grep for walkin/walk-in/checkin/apps-bot/apps\/bot terms, case-insensitive) -- only match is the one generic apps/bot description line already present from REQ-009's doc-update step; still no bot-flow-specific content, so no README update was made -- same checked-then-skipped pattern as every prior bot requirement (REQ-010 through REQ-029).
4. Checked docs/ for an existing bot-command-reference doc (Glob for '**/*command*') -- matches exist only inside node_modules, none in docs/, consistent with the established pattern noted at REQ-018 through REQ-029's doc-update steps, so none was created here.
5. This is the THIRD and FINAL requirement of Phase 6 -- PHASE 6 COMPLETE marker added to the status-history note per the established REQ-014/018/024/027 precedent.
